en.title: Week 7

🧍 Stands alone briefly · not yet floor-to-stand on her own
🤝 Walks holding ONE hand
🛒 Very fast with the push walker
👉 Points at what she wants + calls out
👋 Knows “bye-bye” (not every time)
🗣️ baba · mama with meaning
🚪 Opens/closes closet doors, the toy-kitchen faucet (copied Mama)
🏊 Swims since June · dips under 1–2 s, no coughing
🍗 Prefers bigger chunks to tiny pieces

en.oneLiner: Happy first birthday week! 🎂 She’s pointing to ask, standing alone, and opening everything. This week: answer every point, start “red goes with red” color matching, and practice floor-to-stand. Also: milk in a cup and a mouth-safety sweep (cards below).

bigThree.title: Answer every point: name it, then honor it
lines: When: every time she points and calls out, all week. Aim for at least 5 good answers a day (breakfast, play, walks, bath).
How: 1) look where she points; 2) name it in 2–4 words; 3) give it, or say why not and offer a swap; 4) pause 3 seconds so she can “talk” back.
Say: “Ball! You want the ball. Here’s the ball.” Not OK: “That’s Mama’s phone. Not for Xyla. Here’s your cup.”
Don’t: hand things over silently, or make her say it first (“Say ball!”). Her point is her sentence right now.
Bonus: point back. “Look! A dog!” and wait for her eyes to follow. That shared look grows words.

bigThree.title: “Red goes with red”: start color matching
lines: When: once a day after her morning nap, at a low table or on the floor. Stop when she wanders off.
Set up: just 2 very different colors (red + yellow), identical objects (6 ball-pit balls), a red cup and a yellow cup. Nothing else on the tray.
How: you go first, slowly: pick up a red ball, look at it, drop it in the red cup. Then hand her one and point at its cup. Let her do it her way: dumping, mixing, mouthing a big ball are all fine.
Say: “Red goes with red.” “Yellow goes with yellow.” When she gets one in: “Red with red!” Wrong cup: just say what it is (“That’s yellow”) and move on. No “No, wrong!”

Why it’s realistic: lots of parents online show kids sorting 2 colors around 15–18 months after months of this kind of modeling. At 12 months she’s just learning that color is a thing. Naming colors comes much later (~2½–3+).

Mouth-safe rule for every activity: nothing that fits through a toilet-paper tube (~1¼ in / 3 cm). So: ball-pit balls or 2-inch+ balls, not small pom-poms or beads; big lids or wooden discs, not coins; you sit right there, and it goes up high after.

bigThree.title: Floor-to-stand: 3 tries, twice a day
lines: When: after morning nap and before dinner, barefoot, on a clear non-slip floor.
How 1, squat-and-pick: while she stands holding your one hand, drop 3 balls by her feet. She squats, picks one up, stands again. Let go of her hand for a second at the top.
How 2, floor-to-stool: she sits on the floor, a favorite toy on a low stool a step away. Wait. Let her work it out: hands down, bottom up, push. Help only at her hips, and only for a second.
How 3, one-hand walk: hold one hand at her shoulder height or lower, swap sides, and loosen your grip to one finger near the end.
Say: “Up, up… you’re up!” If she plops: “Plop! Try again?” Calm voice, no big cheering.
Skip: a sit-in baby walker (the push walker is fine).

cards.title: Start whole milk in a cup + mouth-safety sweep
lines: When: milk with breakfast and lunch in an open or straw cup. Bedtime bottle stays formula for now; it goes last (see Milk at one).

How (Week 1 of 4): swap one daytime formula bottle for 2–4 oz whole milk in a cup. Next week, a second one. Target by ~4 weeks: about 16 oz/day (no more than 24), keep vitamin D unless the doctor says stop.
Say: “Milk! Cold milk in your cup.” + MILK sign. Spills: “Oops, milk spilled. Wipe!”
Mouth sweep (once, 15 min): anything that fits through a toilet-paper tube goes up high. Hunt for button batteries, small magnets, coins, balloons. Do the same with her bag for daycare.
When she mouths: don’t yank. Swap: “Not for mouths. This one is!” and hand her the yes-to-mouth basket.

cards.title: Where she is now: body
lines: She can stand alone briefly and walk with one hand: balance is coming fast.
The missing piece is getting up from the floor without holding on. It needs a deep squat and a push through the legs, so squatting to pick things up is the best practice.
She’s fast on the push walker. Great for legs, but walking with one hand or alone teaches more balance.
Heading toward: floor-to-stand, then first independent steps. Anywhere up to ~18 months is normal.

cards.title: Where she is now: brain and words
lines: Pointing at something she wants while making a noise is called asking pointing. It’s one of the biggest communication milestones of the first year.
It means she knows you have a mind she can direct. Answering it every time teaches her that communicating works.
Copying you at the faucet is imitation learning: she watches what you do and tries it. Let her see you do everyday things slowly.
Bye-bye and baba/mama show up when the moment calls for them, not on request. That’s normal.

cards.title: Where she is now: feelings
cards.sub: Confident, but a big change is coming
lines: She’s in a confident, independent stretch: she adjusted fast at the daycare trial and the birthday crowd.
Big change already happened: the grandparents left. She may look for them, or be a bit clingier with you. Name it: “You miss Nainai. Nainai is in China. We can call her.”
Next cycle: daycare + walking often bring a clingy wave in the next weeks (more protest at goodbyes, more night waking). It isn’t going backwards.

cards.title: What real parents are doing at 12–18 months
lines: The most-shared hands-on activities for this age: color matching (2 colors first), posting boxes (coin box, balls into a hole), ball drops through tubes, sticker peeling, poking sticks into a colander (before bead threading), and sticky walls.
Most are DIY from things at home: formula tins, cups, paper-towel tubes, contact paper.
Many posts use small pom-poms and beads. Not for her yet, because she still mouths: we swapped in ball-pit balls, big lids, and big stickers.
Watch her, not the post: if she pushes it away, it’s too hard or too easy. Put it away and try again in 1–2 weeks.

refs.label: Hands On As We Grow: pom-pom sorting + posting at 15 months (mom blog/IG)
The Montessori Twin Mama: 12-month activities (coin drop, ball tracker)
Hellobee: DIY coin box, tube posting, pipe cleaners in a colander
Chinese parent site: 15-month “red and yellow beads” sorting game

cards.title: Do & don’t: pointing
lines: Do look, name, and respond fast. Speed teaches her that pointing works.
Do say “no” to the object, not to the point: “That’s hot. Not for touching.”
Don’t ignore it to “make her use words.” Pointing is the bridge to words, not a replacement.

cards.title: Do & don’t: opening everything
lines: Do give her one “yes” cabinet she can open freely; lock the rest (cleaners, meds, dishwasher pods up high).
Do name what she’s doing: open, close, in, out, on, off. Those are her next words.
Don’t keep saying “no” at every door. Change the space instead (see Our family’s way).

cards.title: Do & don’t: mouthing
lines: Mouthing is still how she explores; it’s also teething. It fades slowly over the next year.
Choke check: if it fits through a toilet-paper tube (~1¼ in / 3 cm), it’s too small to be in her space.
Never: button batteries, small strong magnets (like magnetic tiles with loose pieces), coins, balloons, marbles.
Do swap rather than grab; don’t make it a chase game.

cards.title: Do & don’t: bigger chunks
lines: Preferring bigger pieces is common at 12 months: she can bite off and chew more.
Do offer soft long strips she can hold and bite (banana, avocado, soft-cooked carrot, omelet strips, shredded meat).
Don’t: whole grapes, round hot dog slices, whole nuts, popcorn, hard raw veg. Quarter round foods lengthwise.
Always seated and watched, never while walking.

cards.title: Keep doing: swimming
lines: Dipping 1–2 seconds with no coughing is great water comfort. Keep it short and fun, always in an adult’s arms.
Swimming isn’t drowning-proofing at this age: touch supervision near any water, including the bath.

cards.title: What’s next
lines: Body: floor-to-stand, then first steps alone.
Words: more pointing, maybe a new word or sign. Understanding grows much faster than talking.
Feelings: a clingier stretch around daycare is likely. Same goodbye routine every day helps the most.

daily: 👉 Answer 5+ points: look, name, give or swap, pause
🔴 Red goes with red: 3–5 min, 2 colors only
🧸 Floor-to-stand tries, twice (squat-and-pick, toy on a stool)
🤝 One-hand walk, your hand at her shoulder or lower
🥛 Whole milk in a cup at 1–2 meals
🤟 Sign EAT, MILK, ALL DONE, saying the word each time
👋 Bye-bye when anyone leaves (no sneaking out)
🦷 Swap, don’t grab, when she mouths
📞 Short video call with the grandparents
Brush teeth twice (rice-grain smear)
todos: Get 6 ball-pit balls (3 red, 3 yellow) + a red and a yellow cup
Mouth-safety sweep: toilet-paper-tube test, batteries and magnets up high
Set up one “yes” cabinet; lock the others
Buy a small open cup or straw cup if you don’t have one

quiz.q: She points at the banana and shouts. You hand it over without a word.
quiz.why: Name it first: “Banana! You want banana.” The word is the gift.

quiz.q: She points at your phone. You say “Phone. Mama’s phone” and give her a cup instead.
quiz.why: You honored her point and kept the limit.

quiz.q: Pull her up by both hands so she learns to stand from the floor.
quiz.why: She needs to push up through her own legs. Toy on a stool, help at the hips if at all.

quiz.q: Switch all formula to whole milk tomorrow, bedtime too.
quiz.why: Go gradually over ~4 weeks; drop the bedtime bottle last.

quiz.q: A loose button battery on the floor, she seems fine after you take it away.
quiz.why: Trick question: you did right to take it. If you think she swallowed one, ER now.

quiz.q: Let her open the one cabinet with pots and spoons as often as she likes.
quiz.why: A “yes” space for a real need: opening and closing.

quiz.q: She puts a yellow ball in the red cup. You say “No, wrong one!”
quiz.why: Just name it: “That’s yellow.” Keep it a game.

quiz.q: Use a bag of small craft pom-poms for color sorting.
quiz.why: She still mouths; small pom-poms are a choking risk. Use ball-pit balls.

scripts.when: She points and shouts at something

steps.say: You want the ball. Here you go. / That’s hot. Here’s your cup.
(wait for her sound, then answer it)

scripts.when: Something not-OK goes in her mouth

steps.say: Not for mouths. This one is for mouths!

scripts.note: No chasing or yelling; it turns it into a game.

steps.say: You’re looking for Nainai. Nainai went to China.
Let’s look at Nainai’s photo. We’ll call her later.

scripts.note: Short, true, warm. A photo book helps.

details.title: Why the point matters so much
lines: Babies who point more around their first birthday tend to have bigger vocabularies later, and the strongest effect comes when adults name what they point at.
It’s the first time she uses another person’s attention as a tool: the root of conversation.

refs.label: Colonnesi et al. 2010: pointing and language (meta-analysis)

details.title: Why floor-to-stand comes after standing
lines: Standing up in the open means moving her weight over her feet from a crouch, with nothing to pull on. Many babies take their first steps before they can do it. Either order is fine.

signs.title: 🤟 Baby signs
signs.hint: Comes back every week. Tick the tracker when she watches, tries, or uses a sign.
signs.trackLabel: Tracker (saved on this phone, carries to next week)
signs.intro: Keep EAT and ALL DONE, and add one: MILK, timed with the switch to whole milk. Three signs is plenty for now.

items.name: EAT
lines: How: fingertips and thumb pinched together (like holding a bit of food), tap them to your lips.
When: right before you offer food (“Time to eat!”) and while she eats (“You’re eating banana”).
On her body: now and then, gently bring her hand to her own mouth as you say “eat.”

images.alt: EAT sign: 1, fingertips pinched to the thumb near the mouth; 2, they tap the lips twice.
images.caption: ① Pinch fingertips to thumb → ② tap your lips twice.

items.name: ALL DONE
lines: How: both hands up, palms facing you, then twist so palms face out, like shaking something off.
When: end of every meal, bath, and play session. When she turns away or starts throwing food: “All done?” + sign.
On her body: sometimes gently twist her hands with yours, then end the activity right away so the sign means something.

images.alt: ALL DONE sign: 1, both hands up, palms facing you (others see the backs); 2, twist both wrists so the palms face out.
images.caption: ① Both hands up, palms facing you → ② twist so palms face out.

items.name: MILK
items.sub: Every cup of milk (and the bedtime bottle)
lines: How: one hand in a loose fist, squeeze open and closed twice, like milking a cow.
When: right as you hold up her cup or bottle: “Milk? Here’s your milk.” Formula or whole milk, same sign: it’s all milk.
Why this one now: she’s moving to whole milk in a cup, and she already reaches and points for it. A sign gives that point a word.

images.alt: MILK sign: 1, hand in a loose C shape; 2, squeeze into a fist, open again, twice.
images.caption: ① Loose “C” hand → ② squeeze into a fist, twice.

cards.title: How to teach it
lines: Always say the word while you sign. The sign supports talking; it doesn’t replace it.
Sign on her hand or body sometimes, not only in the air: tap her lips for eat, twist her hands for all done.
Everyone does it the same way: Melody, Dad, grandparents, daycare. Same hand shape, same moments.
Celebrate any rough version. A clap, a hand wave near her mouth counts. Respond like she said it: “All done! Okay!” and act on it.

cards.title: What to expect
lines: Most babies make a first sign after weeks to a couple of months of steady modeling, often around 12–15 months.
Early signs look rough: a hand to the face for eat, flapping hands for all done. That counts.
Signing doesn’t delay speech. A randomized trial found no delay (and no big speed-up either). The real win: she can tell you “done” before she can say it, so fewer meltdowns and less food flying.

refs.label: Kirk et al. 2013, Child Development (randomized trial): baby signing did not delay or speed up speech
Fitzpatrick et al. 2014, systematic review of baby signs

timeline.hint: Each step can take days or weeks. She may skip around.

steps.label: Floor to stand, nothing to hold
1–3 steps alone
steps.note: Toward you, falling into your arms

steps.label: Walking more than crawling
steps.note: Feet wide, arms up, lots of falls

ruler.label: When healthy babies first walk alone (WHO):

timeline.footer: Many walk at 12–15 months; 16–18 is still normal. Ask the pediatrician if she isn’t walking alone by ~18 months.

watch: Loses skills she had: stops pointing, waving, babbling, or saying baba/mama
By 12 months: doesn’t point, wave, or respond to her name
Won’t bear weight, or one side much weaker
Choking signs: can’t cough, cry, or breathe, or turns blue → call 911, start back blows/chest thrusts
A swallowed button battery or magnet, even if she seems fine → ER now
Fever 100.4°F / 38°C or higher in a baby who seems really unwell

plays.name: Couch to Mama
plays.how: Wider gap: couch to your arms, 2–3 steps. Hold nothing; she comes to you. (Wk 4, harder)

plays.name: Wider stand-to-stand gap
plays.how: Two sturdy pieces of furniture, now a full step apart, so she has to let go and step across. (Wk 3, harder)

plays.name: One-hand walk
plays.how: She walks with one hand now. Keep your hand at her shoulder or lower, swap sides, end on one finger. (Wk 4, harder)

plays.name: Playground mission
plays.how: Pick ONE stretch per visit (a new climber, a bigger slide with you at the bottom). Stop while she’s happy. (Wk 1)

plays.name: Bring-it delivery, 2 steps
plays.how: “Pick up the ball and give it to Grandma.” Help with a gesture. (Wk 1, harder)

plays.name: Throw into the basket
plays.how: Balls into a laundry basket: “Throw! In!” The yes-place for throwing. (Wk 4)

plays.name: Point-and-name walk
plays.how: Carry or walk her around: “Where’s the light?” When she points, look and name it. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Pen-book turns
plays.how: She presses, you say the word and add one, then it’s her turn. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Echo-and-add
plays.how: “Baibai” → “Baibai! Bye-bye, car!” (Wk 3)

plays.name: Family photo book
plays.how: “Where’s Nainai? Where’s Yeye?” Pat the photos; grandparents are far away now, so this keeps them close. (Wk 4)

plays.name: Quiet board book
plays.how: No buttons. Point and name, wait for her to point back. (Wk 1)

plays.name: Banana or cracker?
plays.how: Hold up two things. Any reach, look or point is her answer: name it. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Three-cup shuffle
plays.how: Hide a toy under one of three cups and move it while she watches. (Wk 3, harder)

plays.name: Stack & crash
plays.how: Stack blocks together; she tries to put one on top, then crashes them. (Wk 1)

plays.name: Lid lab, harder
plays.how: Lids that pull off, then lids that push on; a box with a slot to post things through. (Wk 1, harder)

plays.name: Freeze dance
plays.how: Music on: bounce. Off: “FREEZE!” (Wk 3)

plays.name: Rhythm copy
plays.how: Tap a pot twice, wait, copy what she does. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Gesture songs
plays.how: Itsy Bitsy, Wheels on the Bus. Pause before the gesture so she fills it in. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Copy-me
plays.how: Wipe the table, phone to ear, brush hair. She copies, then you copy her. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Wipe-up helper
plays.how: Damp cloth after meals; she “cleans” her tray. (Wk 1)

plays.name: Solo play + check-ins
plays.how: 4–6 toys out, play together briefly, then “I’ll be right here.” Smile when she looks back. (Wk 3)

plays.name: Peer time side by side
plays.how: 1–2 babies at the playground or a class. No need to share. (Wk 3, good daycare prep)

plays.name: Messy tray
plays.how: Yogurt, soft noodles or water on a tray. Squish, pour; you name “sticky, wet, cold.” (Wk 4)

plays.name: Water table pouring
plays.how: Cups, a funnel, floating toys. Always within arm’s reach; empty after play. (Wk 4)

plays.name: Daytime night-night
plays.how: Lie on her floor bed together, “shhh”… “Good morning!” (Wk 3)

plays.name: Red goes with red (step 1)
plays.how: Two VERY different colors, identical objects: 3 red + 3 yellow ball-pit balls, one red cup, one yellow cup. You drop one: “Red goes with red.” Hand her one, point to the cup. Any ball in any cup is fine; just keep naming. (from parent posts)

plays.name: Posting box
plays.how: Cut a slot in a formula-tin or oatmeal lid; post big lids or 2-inch wooden discs. Start with a round hole + balls, then the slot. Tilting the disc is the hard part. (Montessori “coin box”, IG favorite)

plays.name: Ball drop tube
plays.how: Tape a paper-towel or wrapping-paper tube on the wall at a slant; she drops a ball in the top and watches it come out the bottom. Use a wide poster tube and balls bigger than a toilet-paper tube opening. (IG/XHS DIY)

plays.name: Big sticker peel
plays.how: Large stickers (palm-size or bigger) on the back of your hand or her tray edge; she peels them off and sticks them on paper. Lift a corner for her at first. Supervised. (XHS 贴纸 favorite)

plays.name: Sticky wall
plays.how: Contact paper taped sticky-side out on a low wall; she sticks big paper shapes or scarves on and pulls them off. Great while standing. (IG/XHS DIY)

plays.name: Floor to stand
plays.how: She sits on the floor; a toy sits on a low stool just in front. Wait for her to get up on her own: hands down, bottom up, push. Help only at the hips, briefly.

plays.name: Squat, pick up, stand
plays.how: Scatter 4–5 balls on a clear floor while she stands. “Can you get the red ball?” She squats, grabs, stands up. That’s the exact move she needs to stand from the floor.

plays.name: Honor her point
plays.how: She points and calls out → go there, name it, and give it if it’s OK: “Ball! You want the ball. Here’s the ball.” If not OK: name it and offer something else.

plays.name: Open–close doors
plays.how: Pick one cabinet she may open: fill it with safe things (pots, wooden spoons, a scarf). Lock the others. “Open… close! Bye-bye, pot!”

plays.name: Toy-kitchen turns
plays.how: Her toy faucet: you turn it, then wait. Add a cup to “fill” and pour into a bowl. Name it: on, off, pour, all gone.

plays.name: In and out
plays.how: A tin or basket plus 3–4 big blocks or balls (all wider than a toilet-paper tube). In, dump, in again. “In! Out!”

plays.name: Open-cup sips
plays.how: At meals: 1–2 oz in a small open or straw cup. Hold the bottom with her, tip slowly, let her set it down. Spills are practice.

plays.name: Bath pour and blow
plays.how: Pour a cup of water slowly over the back of her head (warn first: “Water’s coming… splash!”). Blow bubbles in the water together. Keeps her swim calm about water on the face.

plays.name: Yes-to-mouth basket
plays.how: A small basket of things that are fine to chew: a silicone teether, a cold washcloth, a big wooden ring. When she mouths something unsafe, swap: “That’s not for mouths. This one is!”

plays.name: Mirror signs
plays.how: Sit in front of a mirror and sign EAT, MILK, ALL DONE slowly together, saying each word. She sees both of you do it.

zh.oneLiner: 满一岁啦！🎂 她会指着要东西、能自己站一会儿、什么门都想开。这周三件事：她指了，您就接；开始玩“红的找红的”；练从地上站起来。另外：杯子喝牛奶、家里清一遍小东西（见下面卡片）。

bigThree.title: 她指了，您就接：说出来，再回应
lines: 什么时候：这周她每次一边指一边叫，都接住。一天至少好好接五次（早饭、玩、出门、洗澡）。
怎么接：① 顺着她指的看过去；② 用两三个字说出来；③ 能给就给，不能给就说为什么，换一样；④ 停三秒，等她“回话”。
可以说：“球！你要球呀，给你。”不能给：“这是妈妈的手机，不给玩。给你杯子。”
别：一声不吭就递过去，也别非要她先说（“说‘球’！”）。现在她这一指，就是一句话。
再加一点：您也指给她看：“看！狗狗！”等她眼睛跟过去。两个人一起看同一样东西，词就是这么长出来的。

bigThree.title: “红的找红的”：从现在开始玩颜色配对
bigThree.sub: 好奇 · 每天一次，3–5分钟
lines: 什么时候：每天上午睡醒后玩一次，矮桌或地上。她走开了就收。
准备：只用两种差别很大的颜色（红、黄），一模一样的东西（六个海洋球），一个红杯、一个黄杯。托盘上别放别的。
怎么玩：您先来，慢一点：拿起红球，看一看，放进红杯。再递给她一个，指指该放的杯子。她怎么玩都行：倒出来、混在一起、啃一啃大球，都没关系。
可以说：“红的找红的。”“黄的找黄的。”放对了：“红的跟红的！”放错了：说一下就过去（“这是黄的”），别说“不对、错了”。
心里有数：小红书上很多宝宝15–18个月就能分两种颜色，都是这样天天示范出来的。她现在一岁，刚开始发现“颜色”这回事。会说颜色名字要晚得多（两岁半到三岁以后）。
所有游戏都守一条：能穿过卫生纸筒（约3厘米）的东西不给。所以用海洋球或5厘米以上的大球，不用小毛球、小珠子；用大瓶盖或大木片，不用硬币。大人坐在旁边，玩完收高处。

bigThree.title: 练从地上站起来：每天两回，每回三次
lines: 什么时候：上午睡醒后、晚饭前。光脚，地面干净不打滑。
练法一，蹲下捡：她牵着您一只手站着，脚边扔三个球。她蹲下捡一个，再站起来。站直了，您松手一秒。
练法二，从地上站到凳子边：她坐地上，一步远放个矮凳，上面摆她喜欢的玩具。等着，让她自己琢磨：手撑地、屁股撅起来、往上推。实在要帮，只扶一下胯，一秒就松。
练法三，牵一只手走：手的高度不超过她肩膀，左右换着牵，走到最后只给一根手指。
可以说：“起、起……站起来啦！”一屁股坐下：“扑通！再来？”语气平常，不用大声叫好。
别用：坐在里面的那种学步车（推着走的学步车可以）。

cards.title: 开始用杯子喝牛奶 + 家里清一遍小东西
lines: 什么时候：早饭、午饭配牛奶，用敞口杯或吸管杯。睡前那瓶先还是配方奶，最后才换（看一岁转牛奶）。
怎么换（四周计划第一周）：白天先换掉一瓶配方奶，改成杯子装60–120毫升全脂奶。下周再换一瓶。四周左右到每天480毫升左右（别超过720毫升）。维生素D接着吃，医生说停再停。
可以说：“奶！凉凉的牛奶在杯子里。”同时比“奶”的手语。洒了：“哎呀，洒啦。擦一擦！”
清一遍（一次，15分钟）：能从卫生纸筒里穿过去的东西，全放高处。特别找纽扣电池、小磁铁、硬币、气球。托班的包也查一遍。
她往嘴里塞东西：别硬抢。换：“这个不能放嘴里，这个可以！”把“可以啃的小篮子”递给她。

cards.title: 现在的她：身体
cards.sub: 会站了，还不会自己起来
lines: 能自己站一小会儿，牵一只手就能走，平衡长得很快。
还差一步：不扶东西从地上站起来。这要深蹲再用腿往上推，所以“蹲下捡东西”是最好的练习。
推学步车跑得飞快，练腿挺好；但牵一只手走、自己走，更练平衡。
接下来：先会从地上站起来，再迈出自己的第一步。18个月以内都算正常。

cards.title: 现在的她：脑子和说话
lines: 一边指一边叫，想要什么就指什么，这是一岁前后最重要的沟通里程碑之一。
说明她明白：您有自己的想法，她可以“指挥”您。每次都接住，她就知道：表达有用。
看您拧水龙头马上学会，这叫模仿学习。平时做家务慢一点，让她看清楚。
“拜拜”、叫爸爸妈妈，都是碰到那个场景才说，让她说她不说，很正常。

cards.title: 现在的她：情绪
lines: 这阵子她挺自信、挺独立：托班试园、生日派对人那么多，都适应得很快。
已经有个大变化：爷爷奶奶回国了。她可能会到处找，或者更黏您一点。说出来：“你想奶奶了。奶奶回中国了，我们待会儿给她打视频。”
下一波：上托班加上学走路，接下来几周常会再黏人一阵（分开时哭得更厉害、夜里多醒）。这不是退步。

cards.title: 别的爸妈在给12–18个月宝宝玩什么
lines: 这个年龄最多人晒的动手游戏：颜色配对（先两种颜色）、投币盒、投球、纸筒滚球、撕贴纸、往漏勺里插棍子（穿珠子前的练习）、粘粘墙。
大多是家里东西自己做：奶粉罐、杯子、纸筒、透明贴纸。
很多帖子用小毛球、小珠子。她现在还啃东西，先别用：我们换成海洋球、大瓶盖、大贴纸。
看她，不看帖子：她推开不玩，就是太难或太简单。先收起来，过一两周再拿出来。

refs.label: 15个月早教游戏：分红黄珠（中文）
颜色分类游戏玩法（早教机构，中文）
美国妈妈博主：15个月玩毛球分色、投洞（英文）
蒙氏双胞胎妈妈：12个月教具（投币盒、滚球轨道，英文）

cards.title: 什么门都想开
lines: 专门留一个“随便开”的柜子，其他的都锁上（清洁剂、药、洗碗块放高处）。
边玩边说：开、关、进去、出来、开、关。这些就是她接下来要学的词。
别每个门都喊“不行”。改环境，比管孩子省力（见家庭教养原则）。

cards.title: 什么都往嘴里放
lines: 这个年纪还在用嘴认识东西，也在长牙。明年会慢慢少下来。
卫生纸筒测试：能穿过卫生纸筒（直径约3厘米）的东西，不能放在她够得到的地方。
绝对不行：纽扣电池、强力小磁铁（比如会掉零件的磁力片）、硬币、气球、弹珠。
换，别抢；别弄成追着跑的游戏。

refs.label: 美国儿科学会：预防噎呛（英文）

cards.title: 喜欢大块的
lines: 一岁左右爱吃大块的很常见：她能咬下来、嚼得动了。
给软软的长条，她自己拿着啃：香蕉、牛油果、煮软的胡萝卜、蛋饼条、撕碎的肉。
不给：整颗葡萄、圆片香肠、整粒坚果、爆米花、硬的生蔬菜。圆的东西竖着切四瓣。
坐着吃、有人看着，别边走边吃。

cards.title: 继续保持：游泳
lines: 能潜水一两秒还不呛，说明她对水很放松。时间短、玩得开心、一直在大人怀里。
这么小学游泳不等于不会溺水：靠近任何水（包括洗澡盆），大人都要伸手就够得着。

cards.title: 接下来一到三个月
lines: 身体：从地上站起来，再自己走第一步。
说话：指得更多，可能冒出一个新词或新手语。听懂的比会说的多得多。
情绪：上托班前后多半会黏人一阵。每天用一样的方式告别，最管用。

daily: 👉 好好接住她五次“指”：看、说、给或换、等
🔴 红的找红的：3–5分钟，只用两种颜色
🧸 练两回从地上站起来（蹲下捡、凳子上放玩具）
🤝 牵一只手走，手不高过她肩膀
🥛 一两顿饭用杯子喝牛奶
🤟 比“吃”“奶”“吃完了”，边比边说
👋 谁出门都说拜拜，不偷偷走
🦷 她啃了不能啃的：换，别抢
📞 跟爷爷奶奶视频一小会儿
刷牙两次（米粒大小牙膏）
todos: 备六个海洋球（红黄各三）+ 一个红杯、一个黄杯
家里清一遍：卫生纸筒测试，电池、磁铁放高处
留一个“随便开”的柜子，其他上锁
备一个小敞口杯或吸管杯
看看一岁转牛奶的四周计划
准备12个月体检要问的（疫苗、铁、牛奶）
看上托班第一天，开始打包

quiz.q: 她指着香蕉叫，您一声不吭递过去？
quiz.why: 先说出来：“香蕉！你要香蕉呀。”这个词才是真正的礼物。

quiz.q: 她指着手机，您说“手机，妈妈的手机”，然后给她一个杯子？
quiz.why: 接住了她的“指”，也守住了规矩。

quiz.q: 拉着她两只手把她从地上拽起来，帮她学站？
quiz.why: 得靠她自己的腿往上推。凳子上放玩具，要帮最多扶一下胯。

quiz.q: 明天开始配方奶全换成牛奶，睡前那瓶也换？
quiz.why: 四周左右慢慢换，睡前那瓶最后换。

quiz.q: 那个“随便开”的柜子（锅和勺子），她想开几次就开几次？
quiz.why: 给她真实的需要（开开关关）一个“可以”的地方。

quiz.q: 她把黄球放进红杯，您说“不对，放错了！”？
quiz.why: 说一下“这是黄的”就行，保持好玩。

quiz.q: 用一袋小手工毛球玩分颜色？
quiz.why: 她还啃东西，小毛球会噎着。用海洋球。

steps.say: 你要球呀，给你。／这个烫，给你杯子。

scripts.when: 她把不该啃的塞进嘴里

steps.say: 这个不能放嘴里，这个可以！

scripts.note: 别追、别吼，不然她当游戏玩。

steps.say: 你在找奶奶呀。奶奶回中国了。
我们看看奶奶的照片，待会儿给她打视频。

details.title: 为什么“指”这么重要
lines: 一岁前后指得多的宝宝，之后词汇量往往更大；大人跟着说出来，效果最明显。
这是她第一次把别人的注意力当工具来用，是“聊天”的起点。

refs.label: Colonnesi 等 2010：指物与语言发展（综述，英文）

signs.title: 🤟 宝宝手语
signs.hint: 每周都有。她看着您比、自己试着比、真的会用，就在下面打个勾。
signs.trackLabel: 进度（存在这台手机上，下周接着用）
signs.intro: “吃”和“吃完了”接着比，再加一个：“奶”，正好赶上换牛奶。三个就够了，别贪多。

items.name: 吃
items.sub: 给她吃东西前、吃的时候
lines: 怎么比：五个指尖捏在一起（像捏着一小口饭），往嘴唇上点一点。
什么时候比：端饭给她之前（“要吃饭啦！”），她吃的时候（“在吃香蕉呢”）。
在她身上比：时不时轻轻握着她的小手，碰碰她自己的嘴，嘴里说“吃”。

images.alt: “吃”的手语：1. 五指指尖捏到一起，靠近嘴边；2. 在嘴唇上点两下。
images.caption: ① 指尖捏拢 → ② 往嘴唇上点两下

items.name: 吃完了 / 不要了
lines: 怎么比：两只手举起来，手心朝自己，再一翻，手心朝外，像把东西甩掉。
什么时候比：每顿饭、每次洗澡、每段游戏结束时都比。她扭头不吃、开始扔饭时，问一句“吃完了吗？”同时比。
在她身上比：偶尔握着她的小手一起翻，然后马上结束，让她知道这个手势真管用。

images.alt: “吃完了”的手语：1. 两手举起，手心朝自己（别人看到的是手背）；2. 手腕一翻，手心朝外。
images.caption: ① 两手举起，手心朝自己 → ② 手腕一翻，手心朝外

items.name: 奶
items.sub: 每次喝奶（包括睡前那瓶）
lines: 怎么比：一只手半握拳，捏紧、松开，捏两下，像挤牛奶。
什么时候比：把杯子或奶瓶举到她面前时：“要喝奶吗？给你。”配方奶、牛奶都比这个，都是“奶”。
为什么现在加：她正在换杯子喝牛奶，本来就会伸手、指着要。比个手势，她的“指”就有了名字。

images.alt: “奶”的手语：1. 手半握成C形；2. 捏成拳再松开，两下。
images.caption: ① 手半握成C形 → ② 捏紧、松开，两下

cards.title: 怎么教
lines: 比手势时嘴里一定要说出来。手语是帮她说话的，不是代替说话。
时不时在她身上比，别光在空中比：“吃”就点点她的嘴，“吃完了”就握着她的小手翻一翻。
全家比法一样：妈妈、爸爸、爷爷奶奶、托班老师，同样的手势，同样的时候用。
比得歪歪扭扭也要鼓励。手往脸上一拍、两手乱挥都算。像她真说了一样回应：“吃完啦！好！”然后照做。

cards.title: 心里有个数
lines: 大多数宝宝要天天看、看上几周到一两个月，才比出第一个，常在12–15个月左右。
刚开始比得不像：手往脸上一碰就是“吃”，两手乱甩就是“吃完了”，这些都算数。
教手语不会让说话变晚。随机对照研究发现不会耽误说话（也不会让说话明显变早）。真正的好处是：她还不会说之前就能告诉您“不要了”，哭闹和扔饭都会少一些。

refs.label: Kirk 等 2013，《儿童发展》随机对照研究：教宝宝手语不会让说话变晚，也不会变早（英文）
Fitzpatrick 等 2014，宝宝手语系统综述（英文）

timeline.hint: 每一步可能要几天到几周，也可能跳着来。

steps.label: 不知不觉站住
steps.note: 玩着玩着就松手了（会了）

steps.label: 不扶东西从地上站起来
steps.note: 手撑地、屁股撅起、往上推

steps.label: 走比爬多
steps.note: 脚分得开、手举着、老摔，都正常

steps.label: 走得稳
steps.note: 能拿着东西走、转弯、蹲下

ruler.label: 健康宝宝第一次独立走路的时间（世卫组织）：

timeline.footer: 很多宝宝12–15个月会走，16–18个月也正常。18个月左右还不能自己走，就问问儿科医生。

watch: 会的本事退步了：不指、不挥手、不咿呀、不叫爸爸妈妈了
12个月还不会指、不会挥手，叫名字没反应
腿不肯承重，或者一边明显没劲
噎住了：咳不出、哭不出、喘不上气、发紫 → 马上打911，同时拍背/压胸
吞了纽扣电池或磁铁，看着没事也要马上去急诊
发烧38°C以上，而且精神很差

plays.name: 从腿上走到沙发
plays.how: 沙发到您怀里，拉开两三步，不扶，让她自己扑过来。（第4周，升级）

plays.name: 跨一大步
plays.how: 两件结实的家具隔开一步远，她得松手迈过去。（第4周）

plays.name: 牵一只手走
plays.how: 她已经能牵一只手走了。手不高过她肩，左右换，最后只给一根手指。（第4周，升级）

plays.name: 游乐场小挑战
plays.how: 每次只挑一样新的试试（新的攀爬架、大一点的滑梯，您在下面接）。她还开心时就收。别抱着她一起滑。（第4周）

plays.name: 帮忙送东西
plays.how: “把球拿起来，给奶奶。”配上手势帮她听懂。（第4周）

plays.name: 往篮子里扔
plays.how: 把球扔进洗衣篮：“扔！进啦！”想扔，这里随便扔。（第4周）

plays.name: 指一指，说一说
plays.how: 抱着或牵着她转转：“灯在哪儿？在这儿！”她指什么，您就看过去说出来。（第4周）

plays.name: 点读书轮流玩
plays.how: 她点一下，您说个词再多说一点（“猫咪！软软的猫咪。”），再轮到她。（第4周）

plays.name: 跟着说再多一点
plays.how: 她说“爸爸”，您接：“爸爸！爸爸上班去了。”她的词加一点点。（第4周）

plays.name: 翻家庭相册
plays.how: “奶奶在哪儿？爷爷在哪儿？”拍拍照片。爷爷奶奶回国了，翻翻相册让她记着。（第4周）

plays.name: 安静读绘本
plays.how: 不带按钮的书。指着图说名字，等她也指给您。（第4周）

plays.name: 香蕉还是饼干？
plays.how: 两样东西举起来让她选，她看哪个、指哪个都算回答，您说出来。（第4周）

plays.name: 三个杯子藏玩具
plays.how: 玩具藏在三个杯子中的一个下面，当着她的面挪一挪，让她找。（第4周）

plays.name: 搭了推倒
plays.how: 一起搭积木，让她试着往上放一块，再推倒。（第4周）

plays.name: 开盖子、投进去
plays.how: 能拔开、能按上的盖子；盒子开个口，让她把东西塞进去。她弄不开时先等一等。（第4周）

plays.name: 木头人跳舞
plays.how: 音乐响就晃，一停就“定住！”（第4周）

plays.name: 学节奏
plays.how: 敲锅两下，等等她，她怎么敲您就怎么学。（第4周）

plays.name: 手指谣
plays.how: 《小蜘蛛》《公交车上的轮子》或您小时候的儿歌。唱慢点，做动作前停一下，等她接。（第4周）

plays.name: 跟我学
plays.how: 擦桌子、打电话、梳头，她学您，您再学她。（第4周）

plays.name: 一起擦桌子
plays.how: 吃完饭给她一块湿布，让她自己“擦”餐盘。擦不干净没关系。（第4周）

plays.name: 自己玩，大人在旁边
plays.how: 摆出四五样玩具，先陪玩一会儿，再说“奶奶就在这儿”，坐远一点看着。她回头看您时笑一笑。（第4周）

plays.name: 跟小朋友一起玩
plays.how: 游乐场找一两个小宝宝，不用分享，看看学学就好。（第4周）

plays.name: 黏糊糊托盘
plays.how: 托盘里放酸奶、煮软的面条或水，让她捏、倒、抹。您在旁边说：“黏黏的、凉凉的。”弄脏了再洗。（第4周）

plays.name: 玩水桌倒水
plays.how: 杯子、漏斗、能漂的小玩具。全程伸手就够得到她，玩完把水倒掉。（第4周）

plays.name: 白天玩“睡觉觉”
plays.how: 一起躺在她的地床上，“嘘……”再“早上好！”让她觉得床很安心。（第4周）

plays.name: 红的找红的（第一步）
plays.how: 两种差别很大的颜色、一模一样的东西：红黄海洋球各三个，一个红杯、一个黄杯。您先放一个：“红的找红的。”递给她一个，指指杯子。放哪个杯子都行，您只管说颜色。（家长分享的玩法）

plays.name: 投币盒
plays.how: 奶粉罐或燕麦罐盖子上开个口，投大瓶盖或5厘米的大木片。先开圆洞投球，再换成长缝。把木片转过来对准缝，是最难的一步。（蒙氏投币盒，Instagram上很火）

plays.name: 滚球管道
plays.how: 把粗纸筒（海报筒）斜着贴在墙上，她从上面放球，看球从下面滚出来。球要比卫生纸筒口大。（Instagram、小红书都有人做）

plays.name: 撕大贴纸
plays.how: 手掌大的贴纸贴在您手背或餐盘边上，她撕下来贴到纸上。一开始帮她翘起一个角。大人在旁边看着。（小红书很火的贴纸游戏）

plays.name: 粘粘墙
plays.how: 矮处墙上贴一张透明贴纸（粘面朝外），让她把大纸片、丝巾粘上去再撕下来。站着玩，还顺便练站。（Instagram、小红书DIY）

plays.name: 从地上站起来
plays.how: 她坐在地上，前面矮凳上放个玩具。等她自己撑起来：手撑地、屁股撅起来、往上推。实在要帮，就扶一下胯。

plays.name: 蹲下捡、再站起来
plays.how: 她站着的时候，地上撒四五个球：“把红球捡起来？”蹲下、抓、站起来，正是从地上站起来要练的那个动作。

plays.name: 她指，您就接
plays.how: 她一边指一边“啊啊”叫，您就走过去，说出来，能给就给：“球！你要球呀，给你。”不能给：说出来，再换个能玩的。

plays.name: 开门关门
plays.how: 专门给她留一个能开的柜子，里面放锅、木勺、丝巾这类安全的东西，其他柜子都上锁。“开……关！锅锅拜拜！”

plays.name: 玩具厨房轮流玩
plays.how: 玩具水龙头：您拧一下，停下来等她。再给个杯子“接水”，倒进碗里。边玩边说：开、关、倒、没啦。

plays.name: 放进去、倒出来
plays.how: 一个铁盒或篮子，三四个大积木或球（都要比卫生纸筒粗）。放进去、倒出来、再放。“进去！出来！”

plays.name: 小杯子喝两口
plays.how: 吃饭时小敞口杯或吸管杯倒一两口（30–60毫升）。您托着杯底一起端，慢慢倾，让她自己放下。洒了就是在练。

plays.name: 洗澡倒水、吹泡泡
plays.how: 先说一声“水来啦……哗！”再用杯子慢慢从后脑勺浇。一起在水里吹泡泡。让她对水扑到脸上保持淡定，跟游泳课接上。

plays.name: 可以啃的小篮子
plays.how: 放几样可以啃的：硅胶牙胶、冰过的湿毛巾、大木环。她啃了不能啃的，就换：“这个不能放嘴里，这个可以！”

plays.name: 对着镜子比手语
plays.how: 坐在镜子前，一起慢慢比“吃”“奶”“吃完了”，边比边说。她能同时看到自己和您。
